title: Comprehensive Game Design Glossary & Terminology
author: Jarvis Game Designer Collective
content:
# Comprehensive Game Design Glossary

## 1. Core Loop (Ana Oyun Döngüsü)
The primary operational cycle that a player completes within seconds to minutes. For instance: Action (jump, shoot) -> Immediate Outcome (kill enemy) -> Short-term Reward (coins/exp) -> Progression (buy weapon). A crisp core loop is the heartbeat of player retention.

## 2. Game Feel & Juice (Oyun Hissi ve Tatmin)
Juice refers to the tactile, audiovisual feedback layer that gives physical weight and delight to player input without altering mechanical rules. Elements include screen shake, hitstop (micro-freeze frames upon impact), particles, dynamic sound design, ease-in/ease-out animations, and rumble feedback (pioneered in games like Celeste, Vampire Survivors, and Hades).

## 3. Affordance and Signifiers (Sezgisellik ve İpuçları)
- **Affordance:** The actual physical or digital properties that determine what actions are possible (e.g., a ledge affords grabbing, a door affords opening).
- **Signifier:** Visual or auditory indicators that signal that affordance to the player (e.g., yellow paint or chalk on climbable ledges in modern action games).

## 4. Ludonarrative Dissonance (Anlatı-Oyun Uyumsuzluğu)
The clash between the narrative themes of a story and the actions demanded by gameplay. For example, a protagonist who weeps over violence in cinematic cutscenes but callously slaughters hundreds of enemies during gameplay moments without psychological impact.

## 5. Rubber Banding (Dinamik Zorluk Dengeleme)
A negative feedback loop system that keeps competitions close by giving trailing participants an artificial boost or handicapping the front-runner (classic example: racing games where AI cars accelerate drastically when behind).

## 6. Diegetic UI (Oyun Dünyasına Dahil Arayüz)
Interface elements that exist directly within the game world and can be perceived by the characters (e.g., Isaac Clarke's health spine in Dead Space or map held in hand in Metro 2033).

## 7. Character Locomotion & Inverse Kinematics (Karakter Hareketi ve Kinematik)
Character locomotion encompasses walking, running, and state machine transitions. Inverse Kinematics (IK) and procedural animation ensure feet dynamically align to uneven terrain, avoiding foot-sliding artifacts while maintaining responsive controller input feel. In modern game design, movement systems prioritize immediate acceleration and input responsiveness over overly realistic animation root motion lag.

## 8. Coyote Time & Input Buffering (Tolerans ve Girdi Tamponlama)
Responsive platformer and action mechanics providing input leniency. Coyote time gives players a brief window (e.g. 50-100ms) to jump after walking off a ledge, while input buffering registers early button presses executed just before landing, ensuring seamless action execution.
